title: Amy Adams
wiki_lead:
Amy Lou Adams (born August 20, 1974) is an American actress. Known for both her comedic and dramatic roles, she has been featured three times in annual rankings of the world's highest-paid actresses. She has received various accolades including two Golden Globes, and has been nominated for six Academy Awards, seven British Academy Film Awards, and two Primetime Emmy Awards.
Adams started her film career taking supporting roles in the dark comedy Drop Dead Gorgeous (1999) and Steven Spielberg's biopic Catch Me If You Can (2002) before her breakout role as a loquacious pregnant woman in the independent comedy-drama Junebug (2005), for which she received her first Academy Award nomination. She was further Oscar-nominated for her performances as an idealistic nun in the drama Doubt (2008), a feisty boxer's girlfriend in the sports drama The Fighter (2010), a manipulative wife of a cult leader in psychological drama The Master (2012), a seductive con artist in the crime film American Hustle (2013), and Lynne Cheney in the political satire Vice (2018).
She portrayed a cheerful princess-to-be Giselle in the musical fantasy films Enchanted (2007) and Disenchanted (2020) as well as Lois Lane starting with Man of Steel (2013) in the DC Extended Universe until 2017. She is also known for starring in Julie & Julia (2009), Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian (2009), The Muppets (2011), Her (2013), Big Eyes (2014), Arrival (2016), and Nocturnal Animals (2016).
On television, she played a self-harming reporter in the HBO miniseries Sharp Objects (2018) for which she was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award. On stage, Adams starred in a Public Theater revival of Into the Woods in 2012 and a West End revival of The Glass Menagerie in 2022. In 2014, she was named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by Time, and featured in the Forbes Celebrity 100 list.

Early life
Amy Lou Adams was born on August 20, 1974, in Aviano, Friuli, Italy, to American parents Kathryn and Richard Adams, while her father served in the United States Army at the local air base. She is the middle child of seven, with four brothers and two sisters. After moving from one army base to another, the family settled in Castle Rock, Colorado when she was eight. After leaving the Army, her father sang professionally in nightclubs and restaurants. 
Adams says that going to her father's shows and drinking Shirley Temples at a bar are among her fondest childhood memories. The family was poor; they camped, hiked together, and performed amateur skits written by her father or sometimes by her mother. She was enthusiastic about being in the plays and always played the lead.
Adams grew up Mormon until her parents divorced in 1985 and left the church. She did not have strong religious beliefs, but said that she values her upbringing for teaching her love and compassion. grok_lead: Amy Lou Adams (born August 20, 1974) is an American actress renowned for her versatile performances across film and television, blending comedic charm, dramatic depth, and musical talent in roles that have earned her widespread critical acclaim and multiple award nominations. Born in Vicenza, Italy, to American parents Kathryn Hicken and Richard Kent Adamsâa U.S. Army servicemanâshe was the fourth of seven children in a military family that relocated frequently before settling in Castle Rock, Colorado, when she was eight years old. From age five, Adams trained intensively as a ballerina, performing with the Colorado Ballet and later the Atlanta Ballet, but injuries led her to pivot toward musical theater and acting during her high school years in Castle Rock. At 18, she moved to Atlanta to pursue dance professionally, but soon transitioned to on-screen work, making her film debut as a beauty pageant contestant in the satirical comedy Drop Dead Gorgeous (1999). After small roles in television and independent films, Adams achieved her breakthrough with the indie drama Junebug (2005), portraying a pregnant woman in a North Carolina family, a performance that earned her first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Her career ascended rapidly with lead roles in the Disney musical fantasy Enchanted (2007), where she played the optimistic princess Giselle and received a second Oscar nomination, followed by the drama Doubt (2008) and the sports drama The Fighter (2010), both yielding additional Best Supporting Actress nods. Adams demonstrated her range in blockbusters like Man of Steel (2013) as Lois Lane and prestige films such as American Hustle (2013), for which she won her first Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy, and Big Eyes (2014), securing a consecutive Golden Globe win in the same category. Over her career, Adams has amassed six Academy Award nominationsâfive for Best Supporting Actress and one for Best Actress âalong with seven British Academy Film Award nominations, four Critics' Choice Awards, and numerous other honors, though she has yet to win an Oscar. In television, she starred as the troubled journalist Camille Preaker in the HBO miniseries Sharp Objects (2018), adapted from Gillian Flynn's novel, earning Primetime Emmy and Golden Globe nominations for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited Series. More recently, Adams starred in and produced the dark comedy Nightbitch (2024), directed by Marielle Heller and based on Rachel Yoder's novel about a mother's surreal transformation, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and earned her a tenth Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy in 2025. The film, released theatrically on December 6, 2024, marked a bold exploration of motherhood themes and contributed to her ongoing awards buzz. In 2025, she joined Javier Bardem in a lead role for the Apple TV+ series adaptation of Cape Fear. On a personal note, Adams began dating actor and artist Darren Le Gallo in 2001; the couple married on May 2, 2015, in Santa Barbara, California, and share a daughter, Aviana Olea Le Gallo, born on May 15, 2010. In 2024, upon turning 50, Adams reflected on entering a liberating phase, stating she feels "wonderful" and more open to unjudged personal and professional risks while prioritizing boundaries for her family.
